findings.summary: The HTTP2Shell vulnerability reaches beyond web traffic, with new research showing how the same Brotli decoder flaw (CVE-2026-111497) can disrupt .NET applications, FFmpeg media processing, ClickHouse servers, and Apache Arrow workloads. The findings show that checking Node.js versions alone can leave other exposed software unnoticed. In research published on October 25, JFrog researchers Aviv Engelberg, Eddy Tsalolikhin, and Ofri Ouzan traced CVE-2026-111497 through several software stacks.

findings.summary: The PHP team has released updated Windows builds to fix a serious flaw known as HTTP2Shell . The new packages are PHP 8.5.12-1, 8.4.27-1, 8.3.36-1, and 8.2.35-1, and PHP announced them on October 26, 2026. Each build now includes Brotli 1.2.1, which fixes CVE-2026-111497. Windows users who run PHP should install these packages without delay. The flaw sits in Google’s Brotli library, a compression tool that many programs use to unpack data.

findings.summary: Overview On October 21, 2026, the Node.js Project published a security advisory for CVE-2026-111497 , an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js. The vulnerability affects the Node.js 26.x , 24.x , and 22.x release lines. Node.js rates the issue High, while Google, the CVE Numbering Authority (CNA), gives it a critical CVSSv4 score of 9.2 . An attacker who can supply Brotli data that an application decompresses with node:zlib can corrupt process memory.
findings.title: CVE-2026-111497: Critical out-of-bounds write in the Node.js Brotli decoder

findings.summary: Hackers are now using public exploit code to break into websites that run PHP, and universities and business sites are among the main targets. The bugs behind this wave are two critical flaws in the PHP engine, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 and nicknamed PHP2Shell. Both carry a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.2 and can let an outside user run commands on a server without logging in.

findings.summary: Hackers are using legitimate VLC Media Player and VMware components to load malware onto Windows systems, hiding harmful code behind familiar software. The activity forms part of three malware campaigns targeting users in Brazil and Portugal through fake legal notices, financial documents, and invoice download pages. The attacks combine phishing, hidden scripts, and trusted programs to make infections harder to spot.

findings.summary: Hackers have revived techniques associated with the BlackLotus bootkit to bypass Windows Secure Boot and deploy espionage malware against diplomatic organizations in Central Asia. The new bootkit, named BlackX, appeared in attacks targeting agencies in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan in early 2026. Investigators linked the campaign to APT41 with medium confidence, leaving attribution short of confirmation. The finding was not simply another case of missing security updates.
findings.title: Hackers Revive BlackLotus Techniques to Bypass Windows Secure Boot and Deploy Malware

findings.summary: WordPress administrators often keep their dashboard open in the same browser they use for everyday browsing. A new attack chain shows why that habit is risky. Researchers have documented a JavaScript loader that waits for a signed-in administrator to visit a compromised page, then uses that browser’s trusted session to install a hidden PHP backdoor on the website. The attacker never needs the admin password, because the administrator’s own browser does the work.
findings.title: Hackers Can Abuse Logged-In WordPress Admin Sessions to Secretly Install PHP Backdoors

findings.summary: A newly uncovered remote access trojan called DarkCore is being marketed with a browser designed to reuse stolen Gmail, WhatsApp, and other account sessions while routing traffic through victims’ IP addresses. The approach could make unauthorized account access look like normal activity from an already trusted connection. The Windows malware combines advertised credential theft, file transfers, a reverse proxy, and hidden desktop access.

findings.summary: Cybercriminals are selling a Mac malware kit that can do far more than steal passwords. The tool, called ICMacOS or Icarus macOS, is offered for $699 a week on Russian-speaking dark web forums. It began as a basic data stealer, but its newer version can stay hidden on a Mac, survive restarts, and run commands sent by its operators. SOCRadar’s Threat Research Unit first identified the malware in September 2026 and published a detailed report on October 12.
findings.title: Hackers Sell ICMacOS Remote Access Trojan for $699 a Week to Target Mac Users

findings.summary: A newly observed Windows infostealer called Aokigahara is targeting login credentials and session data associated with ChatGPT Desktop, Claude, Codex, and Cursor. The malware searches infected computers for authentication files and application storage, extending familiar password theft into the AI tools developers increasingly use for everyday work. The threat is not evidence that these AI services have been breached.
findings.title: New Aokigahara Malware Targets ChatGPT, Claude, Codex, and Cursor Login Credentials

findings.summary: Palo Alto Networks has confirmed that a critical Brotli vulnerability affects some PAN-OS firewall deployments and its Prisma Cloud Application Security Transporter Client. Tracked as CVE-2026-111497, the flaw could let an attacker corrupt memory, expose sensitive data, crash a service, or potentially run code without authentication. The company published its advisory on October 26, 2026. The vulnerability carries a CVSS score of 9.2, although Palo Alto assigns it moderate response urgency.
findings.title: Palo Alto Confirms Brotli Vulnerability Impact on PAN-OS and Releases Workarounds

findings.summary: Hackers are using malicious Instagram advertisements to infect vulnerable iPhones with spyware while users scroll through their feeds. A documented attack used a World Cup advertisement to deliver the P7 variant of DarkSword, exposing sensitive information without requiring the victim to tap the ad, download a file, or install an application. The findings show how online advertising can become a delivery channel for mobile attacks.
findings.title: Hackers Use Malicious Instagram Ads to Infect iPhones With Spyware Without a Click

Researchers describe these as “half-click” attacks: users must encounter an infected webpage […]

findings.summary: Two critical Wasmtime sandbox escape flaws, CVE-2026-115889 and CVE-2026-115893, let a crafted WebAssembly (Wasm) module push the Cranelift compiler into generating unsafe machine code. The Bytecode Alliance fixed both on October 19, 2026, and rated each 9.9 under CVSS v3.1. Platforms that compile Wasm from customers or other outside parties carry the most risk, because they depend on Wasmtime to keep that code contained.

findings.title: Fake Microsoft Teams IT Support Messages Lead to Remote Access and Malware Infections

findings.summary: A criminal group has infected Magento stores with malicious JavaScript since July 2025, and 953 online shops have been hit so far. Most of the victims run Magento, a popular platform for building online stores. The campaign is still active. The operators switch to a new web domain every few months, and the latest one, deepveindrilling.com, started loading on store pages in October 2026. What makes this campaign hard to catch is how it picks its victims.
findings.title: Hackers Infect 953 Online Stores With Malicious JavaScript That Evades Security Scanners

findings.summary: Hackers are now targeting the AI tools that security teams use to test their own networks. A new investigation describes automated campaigns that break into exposed panels for Cairn, a platform that gives AI agents goals and lets them work on their own. Once inside, the attackers push new tasks into those agents. These tasks install unauthorized SSH keys, download a remote access trojan, and search for stored API keys.
findings.title: Hackers Hijack AI Pentesting Agents to Install Backdoors and Steal API Keys

findings.summary: Apple released iOS 18.7.11 and iPadOS 18.7.11 to patch a CoreGraphics zero-day vulnerability that attackers may have used in targeted attacks. Released on October 26, 2026, the updates bring security fixes to older devices , including the iPhone XS, iPhone XS Max, iPhone XR, and seventh-generation iPad, according to Apple’s security releases page. Tracked as CVE-2026-86950, the CoreGraphics flaw can allow attackers to run code when a device processes a specially crafted file.

HashiCorp published advisory HCSEC-2026-50 on October 26, 2026, and released fixes […]

findings.summary: Apple released iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2 on October 26, 2026, with fixes for 163 security flaws. The update covers iPhone 11 and later and a wide set of iPad models. The most serious issues sit in WebKit, the engine behind Safari and most in-app browsers on Apple devices. Apple says malicious web content could run code on a device. That is a remote code execution risk, and it is the reason this update should not wait.

That is a remote code execution risk, and it is the reason this update should not wait.
findings.title: Apple iOS 27.2 Released With Fixes for 163 Vulnerabilities, Including Fix for Critical WebKit RCE

findings.summary: ### Impact Agno versions prior to 2.3.24 contain an arbitrary code execution vulnerability in the model execution component. The `field_type` parameter on a `FunctionCall` input field was passed to Python's built-in `eval()`, allowing an attacker who could influence that value to execute arbitrary Python code in the Agno process. This is a code injection flaw (CWE-95) with full impact to confidentiality, integrity, and availability. CVSS 3.1 score: 9.3 (Critical).
findings.title: Agno: Arbitrary code execution via `eval()` on `field_type` in `FunctionCall`

findings.summary: ### Summary An unauthenticated remote attacker can crash a running MONAILabel server or silently corrupt its medical AI inference results by uploading a single crafted DICOM file (~132 KB) via the REST API. The vulnerability stems from pydicom's lack of validation for Decimal String (DS) and Integer String (IS) DICOM Value Representations, which allows NaN and infinity values to pass through MONAI's PydicomReader and propagate through the entire spatial transform and ML inference pipeline.
findings.title: MONAILabel Server Crash and Silent Inference Corruption via Crafted DICOM (pydicom DS/IS Validation Bypass)

findings.summary: Hackers are sending fake FedEx tax invoices to trick users into installing a stealthy backdoor on Windows. The malware, called Sirius Backdoor, hides inside a blank PDF and loads its main code directly into memory, which leaves very few traces on the hard drive. The emails target people who handle bills and payments. They are written in Korean and use the subject line “[FedEx] A tax invoice has been issued.” The message claims a tax invoice of 217,740 KRW is due soon.
findings.title: Hackers Use Fake FedEx Invoices to Deploy Sirius Backdoor and Evade Windows Security

findings.title: Google Guava: CompactHashMap/CompactHashSet/MapMakerInternalMap deserialization triggers uncontrolled memory allocation

findings.summary: The public `/api/remove` endpoint uses attacker-controlled `extras.sam_model` in both SAM filenames and GitHub download URLs. Path traversal plus a URL fragment lets an unauthenticated attacker place malicious ONNX models beside a target file. The models read the file as ONNX external data and encode its bytes into the returned PNG. This issue affects SAM's `sam_model` in 2.0.81 and returns complete file contents.
findings.title: Rembg: Unauthenticated SAM model injection permits local-file disclosure through malicious ONNX graphs

findings.summary: ### Summary An authenticated user with `internal_user` privileges can escalate to `proxy_admin` and achieve remote code execution. The proxy uses one encryption key for two purposes: sealing secrets at rest and minting session tokens. An attacker exploits this by requesting a new API key with a crafted metadata field containing a forged admin credential as the "secret" value. The proxy encrypts and returns this payload.
findings.title: LiteLLM: Privilege Escalation to Proxy Admin via Cross-Domain Reuse of the Salt Key

findings.summary: ### Impact The msgpack-python C extension (`msgpack._cmsgpack`) leaks a decoded map value when deserialization rejects a key with `strict_map_key=True` (the default). Repeated malformed inputs can cause unbounded process memory growth and denial of service in applications that deserialize attacker-controlled MessagePack data. Both `unpackb()` and the streaming `Unpacker` API are affected. The pure-Python fallback does not exhibit this leak in the reported tests.
findings.title: MessagePack: Unbounded memory leak in msgpack C extension on strict_map_key validation failure

findings.summary: ## Am I affected? You may be affected if you use `better-auth` from `1.4.0-beta.18` through versions before `1.7.7` with the Magic Link plugin and social or Generic OAuth sign-in. You are affected if **all** of these are true: - Magic Link is enabled with default `storeToken: "plain"`, or with `storeToken: "hashed"` and global `verification.storeIdentifier: "hashed"` (including a hashed default). - At least one built-in social provider or Generic OAuth provider is enabled.
findings.title: better-auth: OAuth state can be used as a Magic Link to sign in as another user

findings.summary: ### Impact `Snappy.uncompressCharArray`, `uncompressShortArray`, `uncompressIntArray`, `uncompressLongArray`, `uncompressFloatArray` and `uncompressDoubleArray` sized the result array by dividing the declared uncompressed byte length by the element size, but native code wrote the full byte length. If the declared length is not a multiple of the element size, up to 7 bytes are written past the end of the Java array, corrupting the heap.
findings.title: snappy-java: Heap buffer overflow in Snappy.uncompress*Array typed-array methods

findings.summary: ### Impact Several decompression paths in snappy-java allocate an output buffer sized by the uncompressed length declared in the first bytes of the compressed data, before decompressing or validating it. A few bytes of crafted input can therefore force an allocation of up to 2 GB, causing `OutOfMemoryError` (denial of service), or a `NegativeArraySizeException` for declared lengths of 2^31 or more.
findings.title: snappy-java: Unbounded memory allocation from attacker-declared uncompressed lengtha

findings.summary: **Description** def _escape(v: str) -> str: return str(v).replace("'", "\\'").replace("\\", "\\\\") The escaping order is backwards, exactly like the classic HTML double-escape bug: step 1 inserts a literal backslash in front of every ', then step 2 re-matches that just-inserted backslash and doubles it.
findings.title: Flexible GraphRAG: Cypher/Graph Injection via broken string-escaping in FalkorDB adapter (_escape()) - full graph wipe from ingested-document content

findings.summary: ## Summary `OctKey.import_key()` carries the only guard that stops an asymmetric public key from being used as an HMAC secret in `authlib.jose`. That guard is `raw_key.startswith(POSSIBLE_UNSAFE_KEYS)` — anchored at byte 0 — while the loader that consumes the identical bytes on the asymmetric path (`cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization.load_pem_public_key` / `load_pem_x509_certificate`) skips anything before the `-----BEGIN` line.
findings.title: Authlib incomplete algorithm-confusion fix permits HMAC forgery with prefixed public keys

That guard is `raw_key.startswith(POSSIBLE_UNSAFE_KEYS)` — anchored at byte 0 — while the loader that consumes the identical bytes on the asymmetric path (`cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization.load_pem_public_key` / `load_pem_x509_certificate`) skips anything before the `-----BEGIN` line.
findings.title: Authlib incomplete algorithm-confusion fix permits HMAC forgery with prefixed public keys

findings.summary: ## Summary When PhpSpreadsheet loads an OpenDocument Spreadsheet (`.ods`), `Ods::processTableRow()` reads the `table:number-rows-repeated` attribute of a ` ` with an unchecked `(int)` cast, then materialises one cell per repeated row. This value is **completely unbounded**, so a **single ~1.4 KB file** can instruct the reader to create up to **millions of cells**, exhausting memory (fatal OOM).
findings.title: PhpSpreadsheet ODS Reader: Unbounded number-rows-repeated → CPU & Memory Exhaustion (DoS)

findings.summary: ### Summary PhpSpreadsheet's `XmlScanner::scan()` uses a regex pattern that only accounts for NULL byte (0x00) interleaving when detecting `<!DOCTYPE`. ISO-2022 escape sequences (0x1B bytes) inserted between the characters of the pattern break the regex match entirely, allowing DOCTYPE declarations with entity definitions to pass through undetected. This enables Denial of Service via quadratic entity expansion on **all PHP versions**, and XXE/SSRF on PHP < 8.0 or when `LIBXML_NOENT` is used.
findings.title: PhpSpreadsheet: XmlScanner Bypass via ISO-2022 Escape Sequences Allows XXE and Denial of Service

findings.summary: ### Summary The SpreadsheetML XML reader (`Reader\Xml`) scans file content **twice** through `XmlScanner::scan()`, and each scan runs an `unentity()` callback that calls `html_entity_decode()` **after** the pattern check.
findings.title: PhpSpreadsheet: XmlScanner Bypass via Double-Encoded unentity() TOCTOU Allows XXE and Denial of Service

findings.summary: ### Summary A crafted ~27 KB two-block zstd frame makes DecodeAll and the streaming decoder panic with an out-of-range slice index instead of returning a decode error. The same bytes decode fine with the reference zstd. Any program that decompresses untrusted zstd input can be crashed by it. Reproduced on v1.20.0 and v1.20.1.
findings.title: compress zstd: Panic on two-block frames

findings.summary: ### Impact A maliciously crafted DNS message may cause dns.name.from_wire_parser() to use excessive CPU for DNS name decompression. Applications that process untrusted DNS wire form messages with dnspython may be degraded or DoS'd by the extra CPU use required. ### Patches This problem is fixed in dnspython 2.9.0. ### Workarounds There are no known workarounds.
findings.title: dnspython dns.name.from_wire_parser() excessive CPU use

findings.summary: ### Summary A regular expression used to obfuscate URL query strings can consume excessive CPU when processing certain attacker-controlled input. This can stall request processing and cause denial of service in applications using affected HTTP tracing integrations. ### Details The default query-string obfuscation pattern can exhibit excessive backtracking.
findings.title: Datadog dd-trace-py: ReDoS in URL query string obfuscation

findings.summary: ### Summary A flaw in dd-trace-py’s IAST instrumentation can cause the Python application process to terminate unexpectedly when processing certain attacker-controlled input. Only applications with IAST enabled are affected. IAST is disabled by default. ### Details The affected IAST string-processing instrumentation does not properly handle certain internal errors, allowing an error to terminate the application process.
findings.title: Datadog dd-trace-py: IAST instrumentation can lead to application DOS

findings.summary: ### Impact The C extension's BSON decoder scans a Regex element's pattern and flags strings with strlen before checking the document's remaining length, so a crafted truncated Regex element can read past the end of the caller's buffer. bson.decode and bson.decode_all accept mmap and array buffers, which carry no NUL sentinel; the read can cross into unmapped memory and kill the process with an uncatchable SIGSEGV.
findings.title: MongoDB Python Driver: Out-of-bounds read in BSON decoding via a malformed Regex element

findings.summary: ## Summary An untrusted multimodal request can set `mm_processor_kwargs.code_revision`. When vLLM serves a model whose Hugging Face processor uses dynamic `auto_map` code and the operator enabled `--trust-remote-code`, this request value reaches `AutoProcessor.from_pretrained` and selects the Python revision imported by Transformers. This lets a client replace the operator-reviewed processor module with code from another revision of the same model repository.
findings.title: vLLM: Request-controlled mm_processor_kwargs.code_revision allows remote code execution

findings.summary: ### Impact undici's experimental WebSocket client (enabled by default via `allowH2: true`) crashes the Node.js process when it connects to a malicious server over HTTP/2. If the server answers the WebSocket upgrade with a response that fails handshake validation, undici aborts the request, but the abort is a no-op because the request is already marked completed, so the underlying `ClientHttp2Stream` is left open with no error listener.
findings.title: undici WebSocket client vulnerable to Denial of Service via failed HTTP/2 handshake

findings.summary: Reporter: Cavan Loughran, Celvex Group Inc. Summary Authlib's symmetric (oct) key handling accepts an empty key (empty bytes b'' / empty string '') as a valid HMAC signing and verification key. An empty HMAC key produces a deterministic digest that any party can reproduce, so an attacker who knows (or can cause) the application to verify a token with an empty key can forge arbitrary tokens that pass HS256/HS384/HS512 signature verification.
findings.title: Authlib accepts an empty HMAC key, allowing JWS/JWT signature forgery (HS256/HS384/HS512)

findings.summary: ### Impact When an originless `Agent` composes the redirect and cache interceptors as `compose(redirect(), cache())` with a shared cache (`type: 'shared'`), the cache builds its key from the original request URL before the redirect handler changes the origin. The response produced after a redirect is then stored under the original key, even when the redirect crossed to a different origin.
findings.title: undici vulnerable to cache poisoning and cross-user disclosure via cross-origin redirects

findings.summary: ### Impact undici's `Agent` passes its constructor options through a JSON-based deep clone (`JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))`) before forwarding them to each per-origin `Pool`. JSON cannot represent functions, so a caller-supplied `tls` option containing a `checkServerIdentity` callback is silently dropped before it reaches the TLS layer.
findings.title: undici vulnerable to TLS certificate validation bypass via dropped tls options in Agent

findings.summary: ## Impact undici crashes the client process when a TLS 1.2 server renegotiates after the connection is established and presents a different, CA-trusted certificate whose hostname does not match the requested host. Node.js re-runs hostname verification on the renegotiated handshake and destroys the socket with `ERR_TLS_CERT_ALTNAME_INVALID`.
findings.title: undici vulnerable to Denial of Service via TLS 1.2 certificate-changing renegotiation

findings.summary: ### Description `Yaml\Parser::lexInlineStructure()` recursed through `lexInlineMapping()` and `lexInlineSequence()` for every `{` and `[` of an inline collection, without entering the nesting level that the rest of the parser bounds with `maxNestingLevel`. A document made of deeply nested inline collections, such as `[[[[...]]]]`, exhausted the stack while it was being lexed: depending on the PHP version and its stack settings, the process crashed or the request ended with a fatal error.
findings.title: Symfony: Unbounded Recursion in the YAML Inline Lexer Lets a Single Document Crash the Process

findings.summary: ### Description `HeaderUtils::split()` parsed header values with a pattern whose token alternative also matched whitespace, followed by a `(?<!\s)` lookbehind. A run of whitespace placed before a separator could be divided among the iterations of the enclosing repetition in exponentially many ways, and the engine tried all of them before settling.
findings.title: Symfony: ReDoS in HeaderUtils::split() Reachable Through the Cache-Control Request Header

findings.summary: ### Summary A crafted RSA key inside a JWK can cause operations that parse JWKs to consume excess CPU. ### Details go-jose does not check for bounds on RSA modulus and primes before validating them. Values are passed directly to `crypto/rsa.PrivateKey.Validate()`. On Go 1.24+, this takes cubic time complexity with respect to the RSA modulus and primes. This allows an attacker to supply a crafted JWK to consume excessive CPU.
findings.title: Go JOSE: DoS when parsing JWKs that contain RSA keys

findings.summary: ### Impact A Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability has been discovered in the CKEditor 5 engine. This vulnerability is caused by a prototype pollution issue in the `es-toolkit` library used in the CKEditor 5 codebase. This vulnerability could lead to unauthorized JavaScript code execution when the editor processes incoming `style` attribute values. The underlying issue has been patched by the library maintainers, and the fix has been incorporated into CKEditor 5.
findings.title: CKEditor: Cross-site scripting (XSS) in the engine package

findings.summary: ### Summary Atlantis passes the Terraform `workspace` value from a pull request's `atlantis.yaml` into a shell command without quoting or escaping it. A contributor whose pull request is eligible for an Atlantis plan can include shell metacharacters in the workspace name and execute arbitrary commands as the Atlantis service account. This does not require custom workflows, `allow_custom_workflows`, or permission to run `terraform apply`.
findings.title: Atlantis: OS command injection through PR-controlled Terraform workspace enables RCE during plan

findings.summary: ## Summary File read paths resolve symbolic links with `filepath.EvalSymlinks` and then operate on the resolved target without re-checking that the target still lies inside the user's source/scope. A symlink located inside a user's accessible directory that points outside the scope (for example to `/etc/passwd`, another tenant's directory, SSH keys, or container secrets) is followed transparently, and its contents are served through the normal download, preview, media, and OnlyOffice endpoints.
findings.title: FileBrowser: Symlink following escapes user scope allowing arbitrary file read outside the served directory

findings.summary: ### Summary A regular expression used to obfuscate URL query strings can consume excessive CPU when processing certain attacker-controlled input. This can stall request processing and cause denial of service in applications using affected HTTP tracing integrations. ### Details The default query-string obfuscation pattern can exhibit excessive backtracking.
findings.title: dd-trace: ReDOS in URL query string obfuscation

findings.summary: ### Impact Stored XSS vulnerability in the media plugin. Attackers can inject malicious scripts via elements crafted through the data-mce-object attribute, which are created and executed before sanitization. Impacts users of TinyMCE with the media plugin enabled. ### Patches This vulnerability has been patched in TinyMCE 8.9.3 and TinyMCE 7.9.4 by ensuring that, when using the media plugin, any content created through the data-mce-object attribute is properly sanitized first.
findings.title: TinyMCE Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability using media plugin `data-mce-object` serialization

findings.summary: ## Summary MLflow 3.12.0 introduced registration and deserialization support for third-party scorers in OSS MLflow. During scorer deserialization, the server accepts a request-controlled Python module path beneath one of four allowed package prefixes, imports that module, obtains a request-controlled class, and instantiates it synchronously. An HTTP caller can combine this behavior with MLflow's built-in experiment, run, and artifact-upload endpoints: 1.
findings.title: MLflow vulnerable to remote code execution on unauthenticated servers via third-party scorer deserialization importing caller-placed artifact modules

findings.summary: ### Summary On MLflow tracking servers running without authentication, which is the default for mlflow server, a remote attacker can read arbitrary files from the server’s filesystem by creating a model version tagged as a prompt whose source is a schemeless local path. The fix for CVE-2026-2614 in 3.10.0 added a prompt-specific branch to the `CreateModelVersion` handler that rejects `file://` URIs and absolute paths but runs path validation only when the source carries a URL scheme.
findings.title: MLflow vulnerable to arbitrary file read on unauthenticated servers via prompt model version source

findings.summary: A critical bug in open-source EDK II firmware lets a remote attacker run code on a machine before the operating system starts. The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-97631. It sits in the network boot (PXE) driver and received a CVSS v4 score of 9.5. The advisory lists the NetworkPkg package in EDK II master as of September 14, 2026. EDK II is the reference code that many firmware makers use to build UEFI firmware, so the bug can reach servers, desktops, and laptops that boot over a network.
findings.title: Critical UEFI Firmware Flaw Could Expose Millions of Servers to Pre-Boot Code Execution

findings.summary: ## Summary The `/credentials/signurl` endpoint decides authorization from the client-supplied `X-Rucio-Account` HTTP header instead of the authenticated token's account. Any client holding **any** valid auth token (even a low-privilege account they legitimately own) can send `X-Rucio-Account: root` to pass the root-only permission check and have the Rucio server mint a presigned **read / write / delete** URL for an **arbitrary** object, signed with the RSE's stored S3 / GCS / Swift credentials.
findings.title: rucio has an Authorization Bypass on REST API endpoint for signing URLs

findings.summary: ### Impact When the HTML text parser cannot obtain a document from `DOMParser` because the call throws, it falls back to assigning the raw markup to the `innerHTML` of an element created in the hosting document, and the allow-list is applied only to the resulting DOM afterwards.
findings.title: Highcharts Core: HTML text parsing falls back to unfiltered `innerHTML` during printing

findings.summary: ### Impact The filter applied to markup in text options checks `href`, `src` and a few similar attributes against an allowed-scheme list, but accepts `xlink:href` without that check, so an SVG anchor whose `xlink:href` is a `javascript:` URL passes the filter, whether or not the option is rendered with `useHTML`. In the live page the attribute is written without the XLink namespace, so browsers do not treat the anchor as a link there.
findings.title: Highcharts Core: `javascript:` URL in an `xlink:href` attribute survives text filtering and reaches exported charts

findings.summary: ## Summary When `middleware.Static` is mounted globally (`e.Use(middleware.Static(...))`) and an application relies on a **route- or group-level middleware guard** to restrict a path that also falls under the served static root, a `%2F`-encoded request bypasses that guard while the file is still served. This is the same encoding/decoding mismatch fixed for `StaticFS`/`StaticDirectoryHandler` in CVE-2026-55677 / GHSA-vfp3-v2gw-7wfq, but the fix did not cover the `middleware.Static` path.
findings.title: Echo's middleware.Static: `%2F`-encoded path bypasses route/group middleware guarding a statically-served path

findings.summary: ### Impact An attacker who controls the Grid configuration can set `credits.href` to a `javascript:` URL. The value is not validated against an allowed-scheme list before it is applied to the credits link, so activating that link runs attacker-supplied script in the origin of the page hosting the Grid. Exploitation requires that untrusted data reach the Grid configuration and that a user activate the credits link.
findings.title: Highcharts Grid: `javascript:` URL in credits.href runs script on click

findings.summary: ### Impact The pagination language strings are written into the DOM as markup rather than as text. An attacker who controls those language options can supply elements carrying event handlers, and those handlers execute in the origin of the page hosting the Grid when the pagination controls render. Exploitation requires that untrusted data reach the Grid language configuration and that pagination be enabled on the Grid.
findings.title: Highcharts Grid parses pagination language options as HTML

findings.summary: ### Impact The edit mode fullscreen labels are parsed as HTML when the corresponding control is rendered. An attacker who controls the Dashboards language options can supply markup carrying event handlers, which then execute in the origin of the page hosting the dashboard. Exploitation requires that untrusted data reach the Dashboards language configuration and that the affected control be rendered.
findings.title: Highcharts Dashboards parses fullscreen labels as HTML

findings.summary: ### Impact The component language strings shown in the edit mode sidebar are parsed as HTML rather than inserted as text. An attacker who controls those language options can supply markup carrying event handlers, which execute in the origin of the page hosting the dashboard once the sidebar renders the affected labels. Exploitation requires that untrusted data reach the Dashboards language configuration and that a user open the edit mode sidebar.
findings.title: Highcharts Dashboards parses sidebar component labels as HTML

findings.summary: ### Impact A `credits.href` value beginning with `javascript:` is assigned to the window location when the credits label is clicked, without being checked against an allowed-scheme list. An attacker who controls the chart configuration can therefore run script in the origin of the page hosting the chart. Exploitation requires that untrusted data reach the chart configuration and that a user click the credits label.
findings.title: Highcharts: `javascript:` URL in credits.href runs script on click

findings.summary: ### Impact A dot-separated key path taken from `series.keys` is followed without filtering the individual segments. An attacker who controls `series.keys` and the matching point data can use a path such as `__proto__.polluted` to set arbitrary properties on `Object.prototype`. The resulting properties are visible to all JavaScript running in the page, not only to the chart. No user interaction is required beyond rendering the chart.
findings.title: Highcharts: dotted series.keys paths write to Object.prototype

findings.summary: ### Impact When series columns are built from point objects, the point option keys are used directly as data column ids, so the write that populates a column reaches `Object.prototype` and the `Object` constructor. Keys named `__proto__` and `constructor` survive `JSON.parse` as own enumerable properties, so an attacker who controls the point objects can set integer-keyed properties on `Object.prototype`, one per point index, to values of their choosing.
findings.title: Highcharts: series column construction writes to Object.prototype

findings.summary: ### Impact The breadcrumbs `style` option is applied to the breadcrumb button as SVG attributes rather than as CSS, and the attribute names are not filtered. An attacker who controls the chart configuration can supply keys under `breadcrumbs.style` that name event handlers, and those keys become live handlers on the breadcrumb button, so the attacker's script runs in the origin of the page hosting the chart.
findings.title: Highcharts Core: `breadcrumbs.style` keys become SVG event-handler attributes

findings.summary: ### Impact The input-type cell renderers copy every entry of the renderer's `attributes` option onto the input or select element they create, without checking the attribute names. An attacker who controls the Grid configuration can supply entries under a column's `cells.renderer.attributes` or `cells.editMode.renderer.attributes` whose names are event handlers, and those handlers execute in the origin of the page hosting the Grid.
findings.title: Highcharts Grid Pro: cell-renderer `attributes` map written with raw `setAttribute`

findings.summary: ### Impact A custom icon supplied under `rendering.icons` as an icon definition object is built by creating an SVG path for each of its child entries and setting every key of that entry as an attribute of the path, without filtering the attribute names; only the string form of the option is passed through the markup allow-list.
findings.title: Highcharts Grid: custom icon definition objects written with raw `setAttribute` on `<path>`

findings.summary: ### Impact The Highcharts component uses the value of `chartConstructor` to select a function from the Highcharts namespace and invokes it with the component's container element and its `chartOptions`, without checking the value against the supported chart constructors.
findings.title: Highcharts Dashboards: `chartConstructor` is an unchecked lookup into the Highcharts namespace

findings.summary: ## Summary A critical architectural parser differential exists in the `zip` crate (`<= 9.0.4`) between random-access archive readers (`ZipArchive`) and streaming readers (`ZipStreamReader`). `ZipArchive` considers the Central Directory File Header (CDFH) authoritative and ignores the filename declared in the Local File Header (LFH). In contrast, `ZipStreamReader` relies exclusively on the Local File Header (LFH) when extracting files to the filesystem.
findings.title: zip: Critical Parser Differential & Security Control Bypass via Dual-Header Inconsistencies (Zip Cloaking) Leading to Arbitrary File Overwrite & RCE

findings.summary: nodejs-whisper through 0.3.1 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in convertToWavType() that allows attackers to execute commands by supplying crafted audio file paths. Attackers can provide file names containing $() command substitution or closing quotes, which are interpolated into an ffmpeg command run via shelljs exec(), executing OS commands with Node.js process privileges. CVE: CVE-2026-110644
findings.title: nodejs-whisper allows OS command injection through crafted audio file paths

findings.summary: ## Summary LangGraph deployments using JavaScript or TypeScript custom authentication may fail to apply Store authorization changes returned by an authorization handler. In affected deployments, an authenticated user may be able to access Store data outside their authorized namespace. ## Required conditions A deployment is affected only when all of the following conditions apply: - It uses an affected `langgraph-api` version. - It runs JavaScript or TypeScript custom authentication.
findings.title: LangGraph JavaScript custom authentication may permit cross-user Store access

findings.summary: ## Summary happy-dom v20.8.9 makes real server-side HTTP requests to arbitrary URLs when parsing HTML containing ` ` or ` ` elements. This behavior is enabled by default (`disableIframePageLoading: false`, `disableCSSFileLoading: false`). When an application uses happy-dom to parse untrusted HTML on the server side, an attacker can trigger Server-Side Request Forgery by embedding these elements.

findings.summary: ### Summary When `escapeParameter` is enabled (`escapeParameterHtml` in the Legacy API), Vue I18n passes the translated string through `sanitizeTranslatedHtml()`. The sanitizer escapes ` ` in attribute values and neutralizes event handler attributes such as `onerror`, but it does not handle the `srcdoc` attribute of ` `. The value of `srcdoc` is an HTML document: the browser decodes the character references in it and parses the result as a nested document in the same origin.
findings.title: Vue I18n: escapeParameter does not prevent XSS through srcdoc in translation messages

findings.summary: ## Summary When running with the Cranelift compiler backend on an aarch64 target, Wasmtime can compile a Wasm module with more than ~256k targets on one `br_table` instruction in a way that results in an incorrect conditional branch target. findings.title: Wasmtime: Cranelift backend on aarch64 can jump to incorrect target on large Wasm `br_table` instruction

On a host with Ghostscript affected by CVE-2024-29510, this exposes the known Ghostscript sandbox escape through vLLM's image-loading path and can execute commands with the vLLM process's privileges.

findings.summary: ### Summary `fromJSON` and `fromCrossJSON` used two node fields without checking them. - An array node's element list was not checked to be an array. A small payload could set the length the decoder looped over. This part is also tracked in GHSA-wp97-x4hv-qvhp. - A sequence node's done index was not checked. A crafted value produced an iterator that never finished.
findings.title: Seroval: fromJSON deserializer trusts node-supplied array length and sequence doneAt (unauthenticated event-loop DoS)

findings.summary: ### Summary `fromJSON` and `fromCrossJSON` did not check that an array node's element list is an array. A small crafted payload could set the length the decoder used. That length controlled how much memory was allocated and how many times the decoder looped, and it did not depend on the size of the payload. ### Impact A service that passes untrusted input to `fromJSON` or `fromCrossJSON` can be made unavailable by an unauthenticated request.
findings.title: Seroval `fromJSON`/`fromCrossJSON` denial of service via unvalidated array node length

findings.summary: ### Summary When `fromJSON` rebuilt an async iterator, it called `on()` on the iterator's source without checking that the source was a seroval stream. A crafted payload could pick another value as the source, such as a function returned by an application plugin. The deserializer then called that value's `on` method. This is a variant of GHSA-mv8w-475r-vwqw. That fix covered the promise and stream control nodes but not the async iterator node.
findings.title: Seroval: Deserialization invokes attacker-chosen callables: AsyncIteratorFactoryInstance calls source.on(listener) without type check

findings.summary: ### Summary The main Electrum server the client connects to is trusted with mempool ("unconfirmed") transactions. This is documented [design](https://electrum.readthedocs.io/en/latest/faq.html#does-electrum-trust-servers). [0] However now someone figured out a way to practically exploit it: - when the client broadcasts a new tx1, a malicious server can swallow it, - and update the client's history with a conflicting (invalid) tx2 that replaces the outputs with the attacker's output address.
findings.title: Electrum: Malicious server can replace a just-broadcast tx and try to trick user into RBF-ing it

findings.summary: ### Impact When `@sylphx/pdf-reader-mcp` is run as an HTTP server (`MCP_TRANSPORT=http`), it reads the `MCP_API_KEY` environment variable and logs `API key authentication enabled (X-API-Key header)` at startup, but it never validated the `X-API-Key` header on incoming requests. The key was read into a variable and never enforced on the request path. As a result, the `/mcp` endpoint accepted **unauthenticated** requests.
findings.title: @sylphx/pdf-reader-mcp: HTTP transport accepts unauthenticated requests despite a configured MCP_API_KEY

findings.summary: ### Summary JobWorkflowExecutor._exec_inline_python() is designed to safely execute inline Python expressions from YAML workflow script: steps using AST validation. The function claims to block dangerous operations by (a) checking all AST nodes against an allowlist, and (b) providing a __builtins__ whitelist that omits __import__, exec, eval, and open. The sandbox is broken.
findings.title: PraisonAI vulnerable to Remote Code Execution via Broken AST Sandbox

findings.summary: ### Summary Daptin's `LanguageMiddleware` (registered as a global gin middleware) calls `golang.org/x/text/language.ParseAcceptLanguage` on the raw `Accept-Language` header of every HTTP request without imposing any size or shape filter. The underlying parser has quadratic-time behaviour on long lists of malformed language tags.
findings.title: Daptin: ParseAcceptLanguage `_` separator bypass enables >250x CPU amplification via Accept-Language header in LanguageMiddleware

findings.summary: ### Summary A malicious 149-byte ZIP archive can cause a denial of service in applications that enable `legacy-zip` and use `ZipArchive::extract()`. An attacker-controlled ZIP64 uncompressed size triggers a `capacity overflow` panic in the Shrink decoder in optimized builds, potentially terminating the affected process.
findings.title: zip: legacy Shrink/Reduce/Implode decoder: denial of service from attacker-controlled ZIP64 uncompressed size

findings.summary: ### Summary - **Verified version:** zip `9.0.0-pre3` - **Affected versions:** `7.2.0` and later - **Precondition:** The attacker knows (or can guess) the absolute path of the extraction destination The validation applied to symlinks is purely lexical. As a result, an attacker can write arbitrary files outside the extraction directory through a symlink.
findings.title: zip: Arbitrary file write outside the extraction directory, because ZipArchive::extract validates symlink targets lexically.

findings.summary: ### Summary The symbolic-link branch of `ZipArchive::extract_internal()` allocates a buffer using an attacker-declared size before reading any entry data. A 112-byte archive terminates the extracting process with `SIGABRT` through this infallible allocation.
findings.title: zip: Unbounded Symlink-Target Handling Can Abort Or Exhaust Memory During Extraction

findings.summary: In token-exchange authenticated controllers, `shopify_app` exposes shop context through helpers such as `current_shopify_domain`. Prior to the fix, `current_shopify_domain` could resolve to the sanitized `shop` query parameter instead of the shop identity derived from the verified Shopify ID token or active Shopify session. As a result, a request authenticated for one shop could include a different `shop` query parameter, causing application code to treat the requested shop as the current shop.
findings.title: Shopify App: Token exchange shop context confusion may allow cross-shop authorization bypass in affected apps

findings.summary: ## Summary `Challenge` resources under `acme.cert-manager.io` can be created directly by namespace users. On create, cert-manager performs no admission validation tying the Challenge to an `Order`, an owner reference, or an Issuer-selected solver. The ACME Challenge controller then reconciles the direct resource and uses `Challenge.spec.solver` as the DNS01 provider configuration.
findings.title: cert-manager: Direct ACME Challenge resources can bypass Issuer DNS01 solver policy and use ClusterIssuer DNS credentials

findings.summary: ### Description A flaw was found in Keycloak. A remote attacker with administrative privileges, specifically those with `manage-client` permission or access to client registration endpoints, could bypass client Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) validation. This is achieved by registering a malicious client with a specially crafted redirect URI using a case-insensitive `javascript:` or `data:` scheme.

findings.summary: ### Description A flaw was found in Keycloak Policy Enforcer. This vulnerability allows any authenticated user to bypass all authorization policies, including role, scope, and User-Managed Access (UMA) permission checks. By including the configured access-denied page path within a request URL, either as a path segment or a query parameter, an attacker can gain unauthorized access to protected resources. CVE: CVE-2026-9800

Version 0.5.0, the release that fixed CVE-2026-45822, is affected. ### Details When native decodeURIComponent throws, `decodeUriComponent()` falls back to `customDecodeURIComponent` (`index.js:122`). That function: 1.

findings.summary: A new botnet called Kairos is spreading to Linux devices through a very old mistake: a Telnet service that accepts the root user with no password. Once inside, the attackers install a small Go-based program that turns the device into a node for DDoS operations. The campaign shows that basic security gaps still give attackers an easy path in. Kairos does not use a complex exploit or a zero-day flaw. The attackers connect to exposed Telnet services and log in as root with an empty password.

findings.summary: ## Summary `@nx/maven` and `@nx/gradle` spawn their project-graph analyzers through a shell and interpolate plugin options read from `nx.json` straight into the command line. Because a shell parses the whole line, an option value containing shell syntax is executed as a command by any `nx` command that constructs the project graph. Anyone who clones a hostile repository, or who checks out a pull request that edits `nx.json`, runs the injected command with their own privileges.
findings.title: @nx/maven and @nx/gradle have OS command injection via nx.json plugin options

This endpoint lacks origin validation and accepts POST data from any source. An attacker can POST `version[]` parameter which PHP converts to an array. On next page load, function `rawurlencode()` receives this array instead of string and throws `TypeError`, returning HTTP 500 to all users for the next 24 hours.
findings.title: AdminNeo: version-cache array injection causes persistent denial of service

findings.summary: ## Summary AdminNeo allows an authenticated SQLite-mode user to delete arbitrary files writable by the PHP process through the database-list drop action. The SQLite driver validates file extensions when creating or renaming databases, but the database-list drop path passes submitted `db[]` values directly to `unlink()`.
findings.title: AdminNeo SQLite Database-List Drop Arbitrary File Deletion

findings.summary: ### Summary AdminNeo versions 4.6.0 through at least 5.5.0 are vulnerable to cookie attribute injection via the `X-Forwarded-Prefix` HTTP header. An attacker who can influence this header (e.g., through a reverse proxy that forwards it from clients, an attacker-controlled upstream proxy, or a man-in-the-middle position) can inject arbitrary cookie attributes including `Domain`, `Path`, `Secure`, and `SameSite` into all `Set-Cookie` response headers emitted by AdminNeo.
findings.title: AdminNeo has Cookie Attribute Injection via Unsanitized X-Forwarded-Prefix in Set-Cookie Headers

findings.summary: ## Summary AdminNeo inserts the database server's version string into a ` ` tag that carries a valid CSP nonce, without any sanitization. A rogue database server can return a crafted version string that breaks out of the JavaScript context and executes arbitrary code. Because the script tag already has a valid nonce, the browser's Content Security Policy does not block execution. No authentication is required when combined with Login CSRF.
findings.title: AdminNeo Vulnerable to XSS via Rogue MySQL Server Version String (CSP Nonce Bypass)

findings.summary: ## Summary Adminer blocks `ATTACH` queries for SQLite to prevent arbitrary file creation. However, `VACUUM INTO` is not blocked and achieves the same result: writing a database file containing attacker-controlled PHP code to any path with any extension. An authenticated SQLite user can write a web shell to the web root and execute commands.
findings.title: AdminNeo: RCE via SQLite VACUUM INTO (ATTACH Blocklist Bypass)

findings.title: @sigstore/oci sends the registry Authorization header to a cross-host blob-upload Location

findings.summary: ### Summary follow-redirects 1.16.0 and 1.16.1 validate the documented sensitiveHeaders option with instanceof Array. An array created in another JavaScript realm is silently replaced with an empty list, so a caller-declared custom credential header can be forwarded to an attacker-controlled cross-origin redirect destination. ### Details Affected versions The sensitiveHeaders option was introduced in 1.16.0.
findings.title: follow-redirects: Cross-realm sensitiveHeaders arrays are discarded and custom credentials can follow redirects

findings.summary: ### Summary The agent server in `russh::keys::agent::server` never calls `Agent::confirm` before signing with a key that was added with the confirm constraint. That constraint is `SSH_AGENT_CONSTRAIN_CONFIRM` (RFC 9987 §5.2.7.2), which is what `ssh-add -c` sends. The call was replaced by a hard-coded `true` in 3e04597 ("Native async traits encore", #455), first released in 0.50.0-beta.12.
findings.title: russh: Agent server never calls `Agent::confirm`, so keys added with the confirm constraint (`ssh-add -c`) sign without confirmation

findings.summary: ### Summary When a validation was aborted because the document contained more errors than allowed by `max_errors` (100 by default), `validate()` raised a single module-level `ValidationAbortedError` instance. Python appends the frames of every `raise` to the existing `__traceback__` of an exception that is raised again, so every aborted validation extended the traceback of this shared error.
findings.title: GraphQL-core has denial of service via memory leak in aborted validations

findings.summary: ## Summary OAuthlib's token grant handlers can authenticate one client while authorizing the grant type and requested scopes using a different, attacker-supplied `client_id` from the request body. In affected token grant flows, `authenticate_client(request)` sets `request.client` to the authenticated client object, but OAuthlib does not require `request.client_id` to match `request.client.client_id`.
findings.title: OAuthLib: Token grants can use attacker-supplied client_id for authorization after authenticating a different client

findings.summary: ## Summary In pyasn1 0.6.4 and earlier, decoding a constructed OCTET STRING or character string made of many fragments can spend disproportionate CPU time repeatedly copying the accumulated value. A separate indefinite-length `ANY` path has the same problem while collecting the encoded components. The work grows roughly quadratically with the number of fixed-size fragments, although the input and decoded value grow linearly.
findings.title: pyasn1 has quadratic-time denial of service in constructed string and indefinite-length ANY decoding

findings.summary: ### Summary When an application decodes attacker-controlled BER, CER, or DER data without an ASN.1 schema, a container with many distinct long tag IDs can cause quadratic CPU use. Repeated inputs can exhaust CPU and reduce service availability. ### Details ConstructedPayloadDecoderBase._decodeComponentsSchemaless inserts every decoded component’s TagSet into a growing set, although it only needs to distinguish one tag set from two or more.
findings.title: pyasn1 has quadratic CPU use in schemaless BER/CER/DER container decoding

findings.summary: ### Summary `pem.decode()`, which every node-forge API that parses PEM input uses, split messages with a regular expression that takes polynomial time on input without a matching END line, and parsed encapsulated headers with regular expressions that take quadratic time on long header lines. A remote attacker can block the Node.js event loop for seconds to minutes with a crafted input of a few tens of kilobytes. Fixed in node-forge 1.4.1.
findings.title: Forge: Regular expression denial of service in PEM decoding (pem.decode)

findings.summary: ### Summary forge.pkcs12.pkcs12FromAsn1() accepts a PKCS#12 MAC iteration count of zero (or less) from the input, and the PKCS#12 key derivation function then returns a constant key that does not depend on the password or salt. An attacker who does not know the password can modify a PKCS#12/PFX file and compute a MAC that verifies with any password; PKCS#12 PBE-encrypted private keys prepared the same way decrypt with any password. Fixed in node-forge 1.4.1.
findings.title: Forge: PKCS#12 MAC forgery and constant-key PBE via zero iteration count

findings.summary: ### Summary A connection created with `forge.tls.createConnection()` throws an uncaught `TypeError` from `process()` when it receives a record of another content type while waiting for the rest of a handshake message that was split across records. A peer can trigger this with 18 bytes before the handshake, without authentication, which terminates Node.js processes that use the documented socket wiring. Fixed in node-forge 1.4.1.
findings.title: Forge: Denial of service in TLS record processing via a record interleaved with a fragmented handshake message

findings.summary: ### Summary Connections created with `forge.tls.createConnection()` processed received TLS records recursively, one stack level per record. A peer can send one chunk of thousands of small records, such as heartbeat records, which are accepted before the handshake, and `process()` throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`, which terminates Node.js processes that use the documented socket wiring. Fixed in node-forge 1.4.1.
findings.title: Forge: Denial of service in TLS record processing via call stack exhaustion

findings.summary: ### Summary node-forge parses certificate extensions with the deprecated OIDs `2.5.29.10` and `2.5.29.13` as `basicConstraints`, and `forge.pki.verifyCertificateChain()` used the first extension with that name. A certificate with a forged deprecated-OID extension (`cA` TRUE) before its genuine `basicConstraints` extension (`cA` FALSE) is accepted as a CA certificate, and the same technique can hide a `pathLenConstraint`. Fixed in node-forge 1.4.1.
findings.title: Forge: X.509 basicConstraints bypass in verifyCertificateChain() via deprecated extension OIDs 2.5.29.10 and 2.5.29.13

One request with 100 KB of spaces blocks the Node.js event loop for several seconds, which causes a denial of service. ### Details When the `multiple` option is set, the `email` rule splits the value into addresses with a regular expression that removes whitespace on each side of the separator: ```js const regex = new RegExp(`\\s*[${options.separator ?
findings.title: joi: quadratic-time split in `string().email({ multiple: true })` allows denial of service

findings.summary: ### Summary `Content.disposition()` takes quadratic time when a `Content-Disposition` parameter contains a long token without `=`. One unauthenticated multipart request can block the Node.js event loop for several minutes. ### Details `Content.disposition()` reads the parameters with a global regular expression in `String.prototype.replace()`: ```js /([^\=\*\s]+)(\*)?\s*\=\s*(?:([^;'"\s]+\'[\w-]*\'[^;\s]+)|(?:\"([^"]*)\")|([^;\s]*))/g ``` The parameter name part `([^\=\*\s]+)` has no anchor.
findings.title: @hapi/content: quadratic-time parsing of Content-Disposition parameters allows denial of service

findings.summary: ## Summary In pyasn1 through 0.6.4, decoding a constructed BIT STRING with many fragments repeatedly shifts and copies the entire value accumulated so far. For fixed-size fragments, CPU time grows quadratically with the encoded input size. An application that passes sufficiently large, attacker-controlled ASN.1 data to an affected decoder can suffer CPU exhaustion during `decode()`; no conversion or formatting of the decoded value is required.
findings.title: pyasn1 has quadratic CPU consumption in constructed BIT STRING decoding

findings.summary: ## Summary In pyasn1 0.6.4 and earlier, decoding a binary-encoded ASN.1 REAL with a large mantissa can consume CPU time quadratic in the mantissa length. The BER, CER, and DER decoders all use the affected `RealPayloadDecoder`. An application is exposed when it passes attacker-controlled ASN.1 containing a REAL value to one of these decoders, either without an `asn1Spec` or with a schema that includes REAL.
findings.title: pyasn1 has quadratic-complexity denial of service in binary REAL decoding

findings.summary: ## Summary The Kubeflow Pipelines API server decompresses uploaded pipeline archives without adequately bounding expanded data in affected versions. A small ZIP or gzip-compressed tar archive can consume disproportionately large amounts of memory while the server locates or reads the pipeline file, potentially exhausting API-server resources and interrupting service.
findings.title: Kubeflow Pipelines: Pipeline archive upload allows decompression bomb to exhaust server memory

findings.summary: ## Summary The Kubeflow Pipelines API server's `GET /apis/v1alpha1/runs/{run_id}/nodes/{node_id}/log` handler retrieves logs without authorizing the caller against the selected run. A caller who can reach the backend and knows a victim run ID and a suitable pod or node identifier can read live or archived logs using the API server's permissions.
findings.title: Kubeflow Pipelines: Run-log endpoint permits unauthorized access to pod logs

findings.summary: VOLTA is a mature stealer implant with an optional AI-integration layer. After stealing credentials, sessions, and cryptocurrency wallets, VOLTA sends a structured evidence bundle to an LLM to rank the victim’s assets by monetization value. If a model refuses to perform the target assessment, VOLTA fails over to a three-model chain, implying a direct engineering effort and expectation of hitting model guardrails. This stealer is self-deleting, and there is no attacker-owned infrastructure.
